title: [3.13] gh-142664: fix UAF in `memoryview.__hash__` via re-entrant data's `__hash__` (GH-143217) (#143222)
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free in a 4355-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3fae3ac038 in fnv; in fnv; ASan sites ['memcpy', 'siphash13']

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3f923ac260 in fnv; in fnv; ASan sites ['memcpy', 'siphash13']

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion is admissible and is the expected outcome under this guest's configuration: the run records security.cheri.runtime_revocation_every_free_default as 0 and runtime_revocation_async as 1, so revocation is sweep-based and asynchronous, and a stale access reached before the next sweep still holds a tagged capability. Where a sweep has run first the access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). A bounds fault would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial SILENT (spatial-20261006-131005); sublet DETECTED cause=24 (sublet-20261006-123446); cheribsd-revocation SILENT (boundary-20261008-075318)
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-use-after-free (READ 8) at memcpy /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/bits/string_fortified.h:29 | siphash13 Python/pyhash.c:382. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
control_probe_why: trigger.py runs the whole upstream file, which faults at three sites on the physical sublet arm (gh-142664, gh-143195 and gh-92888's test; d3a500f411cb), so no whole-file control can be silent. probe-142664.py runs gh-142664's six tests alone and negative_control.py the same six with the re-entrant release removed; a fault counts by control only when the probe faults in the trigger's function at the trigger's offset and the control is silent.
